_schema.what: The G-ADDR (dial ADDRESSABILITY) floor registry. One committed row per (instrument, REFERENCE), holding that reference scorer's measured end-of-range behaviour on that instrument. A candidate bake clears the REGRESSION tier only when it reaches at least as far at BOTH ends as the ACTIVE reference's row for the instrument it was measured on.
_schema.why: USER RULE 2026-09-04: 'floor and ceiling dial addressability is crucial ... any model that limits dial range cannot ship'. A dial that compresses at the ends cannot serve a target near the ends, which is where near-lossless product decisions live. SROCC is rank-invariant and structurally cannot see this; G1 (p5<=25, p95>=85) is far too loose to.
_schema.keyed_by: (dial_grid_sha256, reference) for the grid rows; (probe_sha256, reference) for the negative-tail and identity rows. BOTH halves are load-bearing: a row is a measurement OF ONE SCORER on one instrument, so reading a peer_ssim2 bar off a shipped_b row would compare a candidate against the wrong mentor. An UNREGISTERED grid or probe is NOT-MEASURABLE / NOT-MEASURED, never a pass -- a bar you can dodge by choosing a friendlier instrument is not a bar.

reference_sets.ACTIVE (bars): peer_ssim2 -- the REFERENCE METRIC. USER DECISION 2026-09-04, verbatim: 'I don't think we should pin to B, ssim2 seems a better mentor.' Direction semantics: a candidate must address AT LEAST the range ssim2 addresses (reach/max/p95/DR/frac<0 >= ssim2's; min/p5/negtail-min/negtail-p1 <= ssim2's).
reference_sets.incumbent (printed, never a bar): shipped_b -- the shipped product dial. Retained so a reader can always see whether a fail is 'worse than the mentor' or 'worse than what shipped', and so the pre-2026-09-04 verdicts stay readable against the pins they were graded on. Labelled BIASED: measured on 2026-09-04 to put A1/A3/A6 ABOVE the reference metric's own values on the same grid (bars 99.98/99.72/86.08 vs truth 98.38/95.46/85.20 -- a dial calibrated exactly to the truth failed all three, and so did both other shipped profiles), and to meet A4 (p5 <= 13.65) only through a -23-point low-band bias (B reads +11.97 on the 221 lowest-truth cells where the truth is -11.30; the train-on-test ORACLE, the ceiling for any monotone re-map of B's ordering, reads p5 21.5-22.8).
reference_sets.not a relaxation: Re-pinning MOVED the difficulty from the ceiling to the FLOOR. ssim2's grid min is -55.35 against B's +3.13 and its negative-tail probe is 100% below zero against B's 0%, so A2/A5/A7-A9 all got much harder. That is correct: the floor is where the incumbent is genuinely broken.
reference_sets.rows without a `reference` field: pre-2026-09-04 rows, all shipped_b. A serde default supplies the label so those rows stay BYTE-UNTOUCHED, which is what append-only requires.
reference_sets.derivation: Every peer_ssim2 value came out of the owner instrument at full f64 precision -- `bake_verdict --dial-peer-scores peer_ssim2=<cells> --negtail-peer-scores ... --identity-peer-scores ... --gaddr-json` -- never from percentile math re-implemented beside it.

_schema.owner: zensim-validate/src/dial_addressability.rs (embedded with include_str!, so a stale or missing file cannot silently disarm the gate). Consumed by bake_verdict's DIAL panel; emitted into --full-json at dial.addressability.
_schema.two_tiers: REGRESSION rows (A*) bar against the ACTIVE reference's value on the same instrument -- since 2026-09-04, 'addresses at least the range ssim2 addresses'. CONTRACT rows (C*) are absolute product requirements. The shipped dial FAILS four contract rows today (C3/C4 negative tail, C5 identity band, C6 nothing-above-identity); those are standing defects recorded here, NOT bars invented for this gate, and the `incumbent` column in every report says so. MEASURED 2026-09-04: peer_ssim2 PASSES all six contract rows -- mono 0.9924, tied 0.0000, negtail frac<0 1.0000 / min -770.62, identity exactly 100.0000 on all 38 refs, 0 of 4,424 cells above identity. That is what 'as good as the mentor at the ends' means, and it is a measurement, not a target.
_schema.append_only: Rows are appended, never edited. A floor is a measurement of a specific bake on a specific instrument; changing it retroactively invalidates every verdict that quoted it. To raise a bar (a better dial ships), append a new row and retire the old one by label.
_schema.record: benchmarks/dial_addressability_gate_2026-09-04.md (section 'Re-pin 2026-09-04' carries the user decision, the derivation and the re-graded candidate table)

negative_tail_bars._what: The NEGATIVE-TAIL bars for G-ADDR. Two pin sets, both kept: `mentor-2026-09-04` (RETIRED) barred the tail against `peer_ssim2`'s own measured depth on the same probe, as rows A7/A8/A9; `product-range-2026-09-05` (ACTIVE) is an ABSOLUTE product bar at -50, graded PER CODEC FAMILY, as rows A7r/A8r/A9r. Selected at run time by `bake_verdict --gaddr-tail-pins {product|retired}`; the default is the active set. A1-A6 are untouched by this and remain mentor-pinned.
negative_tail_bars.user_ruling_2026-09-05: the negative tail bar is entirely arbitrary. below -5-50
negative_tail_bars.user_correction_2026-09-05: i said -50 not -5, codecs are all different, some go lower than others
negative_tail_bars.user_refinement_2026-09-05: A7r is the per-CODEC rule and it belongs on the CANONICAL DIAL GRID (real codec output: jpeg/webp/avif/jxl), not on the negative-tail probe. MEASURED by the lambda-sweep lane (benchmarks/d_peaks_lambda_sweep_2026-09-05.md sections 4-6, commit da0be13b): the probe carries no codec information at all -- its rows are KADIS distortion types (mean_shift, noneccentricity, ...) -- and graded per DISTORTION family at -50 it fails EVERY bake including shipped D and the mentor-fitted arms, on one n=8 family (mean_shift, ssim2 -63.5). So the probe is read POOLED (A8r) and the per-family rule lives on the grid. A9r is REPORT-ONLY with no bar.
negative_tail_bars._ruling_reading: The ssim2-pinned tail depths (A7 min <= -770.619744, A8 p1 <= -187.13142579) are arbitrary as PRODUCT requirements -- they are the mentor's incidental depth on one probe, not a range anything needs to address. The product-meaningful bar is -50, and it is a PER-CODEC question: codecs differ in how far below zero their worst output goes, so a family whose REFERENCE never reaches -50 must not be asked to, and the tail must never be pooled across families. MEASURED on the canonical dial grid: avif reaches -55.3545 and webp -51.8466, while jpeg bottoms out at -8.0450 and jxl at -39.6858 -- so half the families are EXEMPT by measurement. The ruling was minted after a D-peaks candidate (CID22 +0.00798 over shipped D, CONTRACT 6/6) was refused ONLY on A8 -- p1 -167.715 against a bar of -187.131 -- i.e. barred for being 19 points less deep at the 1st percentile of a probe than a scorer whose depth nobody had argued was required. Record: benchmarks/d_peaks_372_postC_2026-09-05.md section 5.
negative_tail_bars._scope: The ruling is about the REGRESSION tail. NO contract row was added, removed or moved, so the CONTRACT tier -- and therefore the board's NOT SHIPPABLE badge, which is contract-driven -- is unaffected by this change. C3 ('some row of an all-negative-truth probe scores < 0') and C4 ('the deepest probe dial is below 0') keep their absolute 0.0 bars.

pin_sets.retired_by: USER RULING 2026-09-05, verbatim: "the negative tail bar is entirely arbitrary. below -5-50", corrected the same day, verbatim: "i said -50 not -5, codecs are all different, some go lower than others"
pin_sets.bars: the ACTIVE reference's own row in `negtail_probes` for the same probe sha -- A7 `min` <= reference min, A8 `p1` <= reference p1, A9 `frac_below_zero` >= reference frac_below_zero
pin_sets.reproduce: bake_verdict --gaddr-tail-pins retired (grading is bit-reproducible; nothing was rewritten)
pin_sets.note: RETAINED, not deleted: every G-ADDR number published before 2026-09-05 -- the gate record's sections 0-15, the 2026-09-04 board grading, and both re-graded candidate tables -- is graded on THESE bars. A count quoted from that era is only readable against them.

axis_definitions.A7r: negative tail, PER CODEC FAMILY: on each family's rows of an instrument that carries codec identity, if the REFERENCE (ssim2) min on those rows is <= -50 then the DIAL's min on those same rows must also be <= -50. A family whose reference never reaches -50 is EXEMPT and is printed as such -- this is the 'some go lower than others' clause. The tail is NEVER pooled across codecs. The row's `measured` value is the COUNT of non-exempt families the dial fails, barred at <= 0, and the per-family table is printed beside it.
axis_definitions.A8r: negative tail -- POOLED negative-tail probe: ONE axis, TWO numbers. The pooled `min` AND the pooled `p1` must both be <= -50. No per-family bar here: MEASURED, the probe carries no codec column -- its rows are KADIS distortion types, not codec output -- and grading it per DISTORTION family at -50 fails every bake ever built on a single n=8 family. A pooled percentile is the honest reading of this instrument. (`min` <= `p1` always holds, so `p1` is the binding number; both are checked explicitly and both are printed.)
axis_definitions.A9r: negative tail, PER CODEC, **REPORT-ONLY -- NO BAR, gates nothing**: of a codec's grid cells whose REFERENCE truth is <= -50, the fraction the DIAL also places <= -50. Reported per codec with its `n`, alongside the mentor's, the incumbent's, shipped D's, Profile A's and D-peaks' values, so the user can set a bar later with the evidence in front of them. Carried on tier `report-only`, which is excluded from BOTH tier verdicts by construction, so it can never block a ship. The companion per-DISTORTION-family reading on the probe is measured in benchmarks/d_peaks_lambda_sweep_2026-09-05.md sections 4-6. Replaces A9 (`frac_below_zero` >= the mentor's), whose bar of 1.0000 was DEFINITIONAL -- the probe's population was selected on ssim2 < 0, so the mentor is below zero on 100 % of it by construction.

provenance.per_family: user-ruling, verbatim: "codecs are all different, some go lower than others"
provenance.product_family_frac_min: USER-PROVISIONAL AND DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED. 0.90 is this lane's proposal; A9r is report-only, so this number is printed as a proposal and barred against NOTHING. Printed per codec beside the mentor's, the incumbent's, shipped D's, Profile A's and D-peaks' measured values in benchmarks/dial_addressability_gate_2026-09-04.md section 16 so the user can set it with the evidence in front of them.
provenance.min_family_n: DERIVED, not chosen, and currently ADVISORY: a fraction at a 0.90 bar has binomial standard error sqrt(0.9*0.1/n), and n = 36 is the smallest n whose SE (0.050) is at or under half the 0.10 gap between the bar and a perfect 1.00. Retained so that whoever turns A9r into a real bar has the denominator threshold already derived. MEASURED 2026-09-05: no codec on any registered grid reaches it (avif 4, webp 1).

pin_sets.reachability_guard: MEASURED, and load-bearing: an absolute bar is still instrument-dependent, because an instrument whose own reference truth never reaches -50 cannot discriminate a dial that does not either. A7r handles this per family via the registered `exempt` flag. A8r PASSES on the measurement alone but may only FAIL when the PROBE'S OWN reference truth p1 reaches -50; otherwise the axis is NOT MEASURED with the reason printed. Probe truth is read from the parquet's `ssim2_gpu` column ONLY; a probe carrying its truth under another name or in another unit (negtail_probe_944_era2r4_foldapp2.parquet stores `human_score_norm`, a /100 quantity) reads NOT MEASURED rather than being silently rescaled.
pin_sets.measurability_today: MEASURED 2026-09-05, and it must not be papered over. A7r is gradeable on every grid with a `grid_family_floors` row -- 2 non-exempt codecs (avif, webp) and 2 EXEMPT (jpeg, jxl). A8r is gradeable on every negative-tail probe carrying `ssim2_gpu`. A9r is REPORT-ONLY by design and additionally thin: only 4 avif cells and 1 webp cell on the dial grids have a reference truth at or below -50, so even if a bar were set it could not yet be supported. That is exactly why it ships as a report.

identity_probes.label: identity_probe_372_2026-09-04 (all 38 dial-grid reference images, ref == dist)
identity_probes.built_from: extract_features_372col --corpus pairs-tsv over the 38 distinct image_ids of the canonical dial grid, each paired with ITSELF, decoded by imazen codecs (zenpng) at this lane's HEAD.
identity_probes.measured_property: All 38 rows are the ZERO vector, bit-identical -- which is what a difference metric must do, and it makes the identity dial a SCALAR property of the bake, dial(0-vector). The probe is kept as 38 rows rather than 1 so that property stays gated rather than assumed.
identity_probes.incumbent_note: SHIPPED B calls a perfect copy 96.2412 while emitting up to 99.9833 on LOSSY dial-grid cells: 266 of 4,424 cells (6.01%) out-score an exact copy, worst `1a20ecb0c1b92466_1022x818` jxl d=0.05 at 99.9833. Standing ceiling defect, recorded as the incumbent's own value.

identity_probes.label: identity_probe_372_2026-09-04 -- ssim2's OWN values on the 38 ref==dist pairs
identity_probes.note: MEASURED, not assumed: zenmetrics batch --metric ssim2 (CPU SSIMULACRA2) over the 38 dial-grid references paired with themselves reads EXACTLY 100.000000 on all 38, min == median == max, one distinct value. So the mentor is inside the registered [97.5, 100] identity band at its ceiling, and since its grid max is 98.3766 < 100 it has ZERO cells out-scoring a perfect copy -- ssim2 passes C5 and C6, the two contract rows the shipped dial fails. The grid truth is ssim2_gpu and this is the CPU implementation; identity is 100 by SSIMULACRA2's construction, which is why the cross-implementation question does not arise at this point.
